standards.name: CI Must Pass
test: Open Settings > Branches on each production-target repository in GitHub Enterprise and open the protection rule.
Confirm required status checks list tests, coverage threshold, SAST security scan, and lint on the latest commit SHA.
Open a test PR with a deliberately failing unit test in GitHub Enterprise and attempt to merge into the protected branch.
Export the merge audit log for the past 90 days from GitHub Enterprise and list merges with failed or skipped required checks.
For each such merge, open the linked emergency exception ticket in ServiceNow ITSM and check approval and remediation notes.
Pass when merges are blocked on red checks and every red-build merge in 90 days has an approved exception ticket.

standards.name: CI Pipeline for All Repositories
test: Export the full repository inventory from the organization repositories page in GitHub Enterprise.
Check each active repo in GitHub Enterprise for a workflow file under .github/workflows on the default branch.
Open GitHub Actions run history for a random sample of at least 10 repos spanning apps, internal tools, and finance batch jobs.
Confirm each sampled repo ran compile and test stages on the most recent default-branch push within the last 30 days.
Attempt a production deployment for a repo with no active pipeline and confirm the deploy gate in GitHub Actions blocks it.
Open the sampled workflow definitions in GitHub Enterprise and confirm build and test stages are required, not skippable.
Pass when 100% of active repos have compile-and-test pipelines and the no-pipeline deployment attempt is blocked.

standards.name: Capacity Planning
test: Open the sprint capacity worksheets for the last four sprints on the team page in Confluence.
Confirm each worksheet deducts planned leave, holidays, production support rotations, and onboarding from person-days.
Open the Velocity report under the board's Reports tab in Jira and compare each sprint commitment to the adjusted forecast.
Trace the most recent externally communicated delivery date to a capacity-adjusted calculation in the Confluence planning record.
Where actual velocity deviated over 15% from forecast, locate the documented re-forecast or retrospective action in Confluence.
Pass when all four sprints are capacity-adjusted, commitments fit forecasts, and external dates trace to adjusted forecasts.

standards.name: Capacity Validation
test: Open the capacity validation worksheet for the intake period under review in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview).
Confirm every approved initiative shows a staffing plan with confirmed availability percentages and no unresolved TBD slots.
Open the capacity-queued backlog in the PPM tool and confirm each deferred intake item cites a staffing or funding rationale.
For a sample of three approved initiatives, trace funding from the intake record to the budget authorization in the PPM tool.
Confirm each sampled initiative received a budget code or cost-center authorization dated before project kick-off.
Pass when no approved initiative has a TBD slot, all deferred items carry capacity rationale, and all three fundings trace.

standards.name: Change Data Capture for Real-Time
test: Open the pipeline configuration repo in GitHub Enterprise for each near-real-time feed such as claims status and fraud screening.
Confirm each feed uses a CDC mechanism (log-based, trigger-based, or outbox) rather than high-frequency batch queries.
Open the CDC connector configuration in Kafka Connect and confirm DELETE and schema-change events are captured, not discarded.
Open the replication-lag dashboard in Grafana and confirm an active lag alert threshold with a recent lag metric recorded.
Check the alerting ruleset in Grafana and confirm lag threshold breaches route to an incident notification.
Pass when every near-real-time feed uses CDC with delete and schema-change handling and an active replication-lag alert.

standards.name: Changelog Maintained
test: Open the versioned changelog file in each API repository in GitHub Enterprise.
Compare changelog entries to the release tag list in GitHub Enterprise and confirm no release version is absent.
Confirm entries label additions, deprecations, and breaking changes distinctly for each release.
For the 3 most recent deprecations, compare the changelog commit dates in GitHub Enterprise to the removal release dates.
Check the API versioning policy in Confluence and confirm each notice met the full deprecation-notice period before removal.
Survey one internal and one external consumer team and record whether each planned upgrade work from the changelog alone.
Pass when no release is missing, all 3 deprecations met the notice period, and both consumers relied on the changelog alone.

standards.name: Completeness Above 99%
test: Open the completeness rule set for each governed dataset in Collibra Data Quality.
Confirm every defined critical data element has a completeness rule configured with a 99% pass threshold.
Export the most recent completeness results from Collibra Data Quality and compute the pass rate per critical field.
Open the quality dashboard in Collibra and list any datasets flagged below the 99% threshold.
For each flagged dataset, open its remediation ticket in ServiceNow ITSM and confirm an assigned owner and due date.
Review the dashboard access list in Collibra and confirm owner, steward, and consumer groups all have visibility.
Pass when all critical fields exceed 99% populated and every flagged dataset has an open remediation record with owner and date.

standards.name: Complex Logic Commented
test: Run a code search in GitHub Enterprise for premium, reinsurance, state, rate, and filing keywords across in-scope repos.
Open each matching method and confirm an inline comment explains the business rationale, not line-by-line mechanics.
For a sample of five commented blocks, verify the comment cites a source requirement, regulatory filing, or product spec.
Open a test pull request in GitHub Enterprise changing a complex-logic block without a qualifying comment.
Confirm the review checklist or automated lint rule in GitHub Actions blocks or flags the merge.
Pass when all five sampled blocks carry rationale comments with citations and the uncommented PR is flagged or blocked.

standards.name: Conceptual, Logical, and Physical Models Required
test: List significant data initiatives active or completed in the past 12 months in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview).
Open each initiative's design-gate space in Confluence and locate the conceptual, logical, and physical model documents.
Trace every conceptual entity to a logical entity and every logical entity to a physical table, logging any gap as a finding.
Open the gate review minutes or ADR approvals in Confluence and confirm each model level was signed off at its design gate.
Pass when every initiative has all three models with full entity traceability and recorded sign-off at each gate.

standards.name: Consistent Dev, Test, and Prod Environments
test: Open the infrastructure-as-code templates and image manifests in GitHub Enterprise for dev, test, and prod.
Compare OS image tags, runtime versions, and middleware versions across the three tiers and record every difference.
Query the CMDB in ServiceNow ITSM for each environment's network topology and verify parity beyond scale parameters.
Open the deviation register in Confluence and confirm each entry has justification, reviewer approval, and a remediation date.
Flag any difference found in the comparisons that is absent from the deviation register as a control failure.
Open the last release certification for a policy or claims system in Confluence and check the reproducibility attestation.
Pass when stack versions match across tiers, all deviations are registered and reviewed, and the certification attests parity.

standards.name: Consumer-Driven Contracts
test: Open the Pact Broker and confirm every known consuming team of each in-scope API has published at least one contract.
For the policy administration API, compare the provider interface in the Pact Broker against the union of registered contracts.
On a test branch in GitHub Enterprise, remove a required response field from the policy administration API.
Run provider verification in GitHub Actions and confirm every dependent consumer contract fails before the deploy gate.
Open the onboarding checklist for a recently integrated consumer in Confluence and confirm its contract predates staging.
Pass when all consumers have contracts, the breaking change fails verification, and the new consumer registered before staging.

standards.name: Contract Testing in CI/CD
test: Open the provider pipeline workflow in GitHub Actions and confirm a contract-test stage fetches broker contracts before deploy.
Open the most recent provider run log in GitHub Actions and confirm verification executed against all consumer contracts.
Locate the most recent failed contract verification in the GitHub Actions run history.
Confirm in GitHub Actions that the failed build promoted no artifact to staging or production.
Open a consumer pipeline such as the agent portal in GitHub Actions and confirm it verifies the provider's published contract.
Pass when both provider and consumer pipelines run mandatory contract stages and the failed verification blocked promotion.

standards.name: Contract Tests for APIs
test: Open the Pact Broker and confirm every active API has a registered consumer contract with a passing latest verification.
Open the provider and at least two consumer pipeline workflows in GitHub Actions and confirm verification is a required stage.
Push a deliberate breaking schema change to the provider API on a test branch in GitHub Enterprise.
Confirm the provider pipeline in GitHub Actions fails at contract verification and names the violated consumer contract.
Filter the Pact Broker verification matrix to the last 30 days and check for deployments with unverified or failing contracts.
Pass when all contracts verify green on both sides, the stage is non-skippable, and no 30-day deploy had failing contracts.

standards.name: Dashboards per Service
test: Export the production service inventory from the CMDB in ServiceNow ITSM.
Open Grafana and confirm a dedicated dashboard exists for every inventoried production service, flagging any gap.
For three sampled dashboards including a claims-facing and an underwriting-facing service, check RED and utilization panels.
Confirm each sampled dashboard in Grafana also shows a business indicator such as quotes issued or claims processed.
Compare five dashboards in Grafana against the approved common template for section order, panel naming, and thresholds.
Check last-modified dates in Grafana against each service's last deployment, flagging dashboards unedited beyond 90 days.
Pass when every service has a dashboard, sampled panels are complete, layouts match the template, and none are stale past 90 days.

standards.name: Data Contracts Enforced
test: For five sampled pipelines spanning claims, policy, and billing feeds, open each contract artifact in the schema registry.
Confirm each contract specifies field types, nullability, and key constraints agreed with the producing system team.
Replay a load with a deliberate violation, such as a null in a non-nullable field, in a non-production pipeline environment.
Confirm the pipeline quarantines the record or halts the load and no violated record reaches the downstream target table.
Search the last 30 days of run logs in the pipeline orchestrator (Airflow) for violations with record-level detail logged.
Pass when all five contracts are complete, the injected violation is quarantined or halted, and dispositions match criticality.

standards.name: Data Quality Scores Published
test: Open the enterprise data quality dashboard in Collibra and confirm composite scores display per dataset and per domain.
Open sampled dataset detail pages in the Collibra data catalog and confirm the quality scores surface there.
Retrieve governance forum minutes for the prior two quarters from Confluence and confirm quality trends were reviewed in both.
Identify domains below threshold for two or more consecutive periods and open each remediation plan in Confluence.
Confirm each plan names an owner and target date, then review Collibra access roles for owner, steward, and consumer groups.
Pass when scores publish in dashboard and catalog, both quarters show trend review, and each low-scoring domain has a plan.

standards.name: Data Validation
test: Open the latest premium, reserve, and claims report releases and their tie-out workbooks in SharePoint.
Compare each report total to the source-system extract or general ledger and confirm variance within the documented tolerance.
Confirm each workbook sits in the designated SharePoint repository with a version stamp matching the report release date.
Cross-check reserve totals in one actuarial report against the actuarial control schedule such as the IBNR summary sign-off.
Confirm any reconciliation differences carry a documented explanation and recorded approval in the workbook.
Pass when every report total ties out within tolerance and each release retains a version-stamped, signed tie-out workbook.

standards.name: Debt Ratio Below 15 Percent of Velocity
test: Open the Velocity report under the board's Reports tab in Jira for the last three completed sprints.
Calculate each sprint's debt-remediation story-point ratio from the Jira sprint reports and compare to the 15% ceiling.
For any sprint at or above 12%, locate the documented feature-intake throttle decision (label or board policy note) in Jira.
Open the sprint planning notes in Confluence and confirm a written threshold-monitoring practice with pre-sprint sign-off.
Pass when no sprint exceeds 15%, every near-ceiling sprint shows an enacted throttle decision, and sign-offs are recorded.
